'''''Acutodon''''' ({{lit|sharp, pointed teeth}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of [[shinisauria]]n lizard that lived in [[France]] during the [[Late Cretaceous]] (lower [[Campanian]] age). The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Acutodon villeveyracensis''''', known from a partial [[maxilla]] (upper tooth-bearing bone). Acutodon lived in freshwater subtropical environments.<ref name="Acutodon" />

== Description ==
It is characterized by its long, tapering teeth, which suggest a diet of small [[fish]] and [[Amphibian|amphibians]]. This is comparable to the modern [[Chinese crocodile lizard]] (''Shinisaurus crocodilurus'').<ref name="Acutodon" />

== Phylogeny ==
Acutodon is a [[Shinisauria|Pan-Shinisauria]], a clade of [[Anguimorpha|Anguimorph]] lizards that contains genera such as ''[[Merkurosaurus]]'' from the [[Czech Republic]].<ref>Klembara, Jozef. (2008). A new anguimorph lizard from the Lower Miocene of North-West Bohemia, Czech Republic. Palaeontology. 51. 81 - 94. 10.1111/j.1475-4983.2007.00732.x. </ref> The closest living relative to Acutodon is the [[Chinese crocodile lizard]]. The evolutionary history of this clade is poorly known with few fossils being found. This genus fills in a gap in the fossil record of Pan-Shinisaurids.<ref name="Acutodon" />
